need: stop people from plugging their own hubs or extra devices into the wall jacks of the access switches
clues: each wall jack should serve only the one desk computer that is already connected to it
the switches are managed models
staff have been adding small unmanaged hubs under their desks
the switch should shut the jack down or send an alert when a new device shows up

answer.item: Port security with a MAC address limit

appliesWhen: each switch port must accept only one or a few known hardware addresses
explanation: Port security works at Layer 2 and lets a switch port accept only the hardware addresses it has learned or been given. When another device appears, the switch can shut the port, send an SNMP trap, or send an alert.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

need: make every wired and wireless device prove who it is before the switch or access point lets it on the network
clues: a RADIUS server is already running for the VPN
the switches and access points should not do the checking themselves
the company wants to use digital certificates on each laptop
an unknown device that connects to a port must get no network access

answer.item: 802.1X port-based authentication with an authentication server

appliesWhen: each device must authenticate through EAP to a central server before its port opens
explanation: 802.1X carries EAP between the device, the switch or access point, and a central authentication server, so the network devices only pass the request on. Certificate-based EAP-TLS is its most secure form.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

need: let only the store's three tablets and its printer join the small wireless network
clues: the access point is a basic small-office model with no RADIUS support
the list of allowed devices rarely changes
the owner has written down the hardware address of each device
a simple allow list is enough for this small site

answer.item: MAC filtering with an allow list on the access point

appliesWhen: a small fixed set of devices is allowed by hardware address on a basic access point
explanation: MAC filtering keeps an allow or deny list of hardware addresses, and the access point rejects any adapter that is not on the allow list. It is simple for a small fixed set of devices, though addresses can be spoofed.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

need: keep laptops with old antivirus definitions or missing patches off the production network
clues: each laptop must be checked for its security settings when it connects
a laptop that fails the check should go to a quarantine network until it is fixed
the check should read the antivirus version and the patch level
a temporary agent can run on visitor devices

answer.item: Network access control (NAC) with a posture assessment

appliesWhen: each device's security state must be checked before it gets access, with failures sent to quarantine
explanation: NAC gathers information from the device, such as its antivirus version and patch level, and decides what access it gets. A device that fails the posture assessment can be placed in a quarantine network.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

need: give visitors Internet access only after they accept the acceptable use policy
clues: visitors use their own phones and laptops
a web page should open first when a visitor connects
visitors must agree to the terms before they can browse
no software should be installed on visitor devices

answer.item: A captive portal on the guest wireless network

appliesWhen: guests must view a web page and agree to terms before they get Internet access
explanation: A captive portal is the web page a guest sees first on a public network, and it holds back other access until the user acts, such as accepting the AUP. Coffee shops, hospitals, and hotels use it for guest Wi-Fi.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

need: keep visitors on the wireless network from seeing or reaching each other's devices and the staff computers
clues: visitors only need to reach the Internet
a visitor's laptop should not be able to find any other connected device
the staff file shares must stay out of reach
the access point can run a second wireless network for visitors

answer.item: Guest network isolation on a separate guest wireless network

appliesWhen: guest users must reach the Internet but no other connected devices
explanation: With guest network isolation, guest users get to the Internet but cannot see any other connected devices. The guest network is treated as an untrusted zone, apart from the staff network.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

need: stop one outside address that keeps scanning the network from reaching it at all
clues: the scans come from the same public IP address every night
the edge router can filter traffic by source address
all other outside traffic must keep working
the block should be applied at the network edge

answer.item: An access control list (ACL) entry on the edge router that denies that source

appliesWhen: traffic from a specific address must be rejected at the router
explanation: An ACL lets a router ignore or reject requests from specified addresses while other traffic passes. A deny entry for the scanning address drops its traffic every time it arrives.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

need: block staff from gambling and social media websites while other web browsing keeps working
clues: the acceptable use policy names categories of sites that are not allowed
new sites in those categories appear every week
the rules should apply to whole groups of websites, not single IP addresses
the school's web proxy has a subscription to a site reputation list
appliesWhen: access to websites must be allowed or blocked by address or category
explanation: URL filtering, also called web filtering, allows or blocks websites by their address, category, or reputation. Blocking by category keeps up with new sites without a rule for each one.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

need: stop emails and downloads that carry malware or customer card numbers from passing through
clues: the inspection must look inside messages and files, not only at their addresses
outgoing messages that contain sensitive data must be held
spam should be removed before it reaches the inboxes
the mail server and the firewall can both inspect traffic

answer.item: Content filtering on the mail server and firewall

appliesWhen: the data inside messages, files, and pages must be inspected and filtered
explanation: Content filtering inspects packets, files, emails, and web content and removes unwanted items such as malware, spam, or sensitive data. Firewalls, mail servers, and DNS servers can all do it.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

need: host a public web server so Internet users can reach it without giving them a path into the internal LAN
clues: customers on the Internet must reach the web server
the web server should not sit on the same segment as the staff computers
all traffic to and from the server must pass through the firewall
an attacker who takes over the web server must still face another barrier

answer.item: A screened subnet (formerly a DMZ) behind the firewall

appliesWhen: servers must be reached from both outside and inside but sit on neither network
explanation: A screened subnet holds servers that both outside and inside users must reach, and it is reached only through the firewall. An intruder on that segment still has to get past the firewall to reach the internal network.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

need: make sure the firewall drops any traffic that no rule has allowed
clues: the firewall has permit rules only for web, mail, and VPN traffic
an audit found traffic on other ports passing through
new services should be blocked until someone adds a rule for them
the policy is least privilege

answer.item: An implicit deny rule at the end of the rule set

appliesWhen: everything that is not allowed by an earlier rule must be blocked
explanation: An implicit deny at the end of the rule set blocks anything an earlier rule has not allowed. New or unknown traffic then stays blocked until a permit rule is added.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

need: decide where to put the partner company's network connection in the firewall design
clues: the partner network is outside the company's direct control
the partner needs only one application on one server
stricter firewall rules and access lists must apply to this traffic
the internal staff network must stay off-limits to the partner

answer.item: The untrusted zone, with access only to that one server

appliesWhen: a network outside the company's direct control must face strict rules before reaching internal resources
explanation: Networks outside the company's control, such as the Internet, guest Wi-Fi, and partner networks, belong in the untrusted zone. Traffic from that zone faces stricter firewall rules and reaches only the resources it needs.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: the router's logs show a successful admin login from the Internet
nobody on the staff made the login
the router was set up last month exactly as it came out of the box
the login used the vendor's standard admin account name

answer.cause: the factory default admin credentials were never changed
answer.action: Change the default username and password to a unique, complex one

firstStep: Check whether the router still accepts the vendor's standard login
appliesWhen: the device still accepts the login values it shipped with
explanation: Anyone who owns the same model knows its factory login, so a device left as it came out of the box is easy to enter. The default account values must be changed as soon as the device goes into use.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: a visitor's laptop got a network address from a jack in the empty conference room
nobody has used that room's jacks for a year
the switch shows a link light on a port that maps to the room
every switch port is in the active state

answer.cause: unused switch ports were left enabled
answer.action: Disable every switch port that is not in use

firstStep: Check the switch for active ports that map to unused jacks
appliesWhen: ports with nothing assigned to them are still active and give a way in
explanation: An unused port that stays active is an open door: anyone who plugs in gets on the network. Disabling physical and virtual ports that are not needed shrinks the attack surface.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: a vulnerability scan of the file server lists Telnet, FTP, and a print spooler
the server only shares files
the scan rates the server as high risk
the server was built from the vendor's full default install

answer.cause: services the server does not need are still running
answer.action: Disable or remove every service the server does not use

firstStep: List the services that are running on the server
appliesWhen: a host runs programs that its role does not need
explanation: Each running service is another door into the server. Removing the ones its role does not use reduces the attack surface and the overhead.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: one switch's admin password was leaked by a former contractor
within a day an attacker had logged in to routers and switches at three sites
the defaults were changed when the devices were installed
the same short word is used for every device's admin login

answer.cause: one simple password is reused on every network device
answer.action: Set a long, complex, and different password on each device

appliesWhen: one leaked admin password opens every device because all of them share it
explanation: When all devices share one simple password, a single leak opens every device. Each device needs its own long, complex password.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: the vendor published a security notice about the router model last year
attackers are using a known flaw in that model
the passwords and port settings follow the hardening checklist
the router reports the same version it had when it was bought

answer.cause: the device's firmware is out of date and still has a known security flaw
answer.action: Test the vendor's latest firmware in the lab, then install it on the router

firstStep: Compare the router's version with the vendor's latest release
appliesWhen: the device runs an old version with a flaw the vendor has already fixed
explanation: Firmware updates often fix security flaws, so an old version keeps holes the vendor has already closed. The update should be tested on a lab device first and then installed.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: the VPN uses the same pre-shared secret it was set up with five years ago
a dozen former staff members knew the secret
there is no schedule for changing it
traffic captures show a stranger connected to the VPN

answer.cause: the key has been in use for years with no rotation
answer.action: Generate new keys and change them on a regular schedule

appliesWhen: a key stays in use so long that the window to crack or leak it keeps growing
explanation: The longer one key stays in use, the more chances there are for it to be cracked or leaked. Regular rotation limits how long a stolen key works.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: a laptop with a client certificate was stolen last week
the thief's laptop can still sign in to the wireless network
the certificate is valid for two more years
nobody updated the CRL after the theft

answer.cause: the stolen laptop's certificate and key were never revoked
answer.action: Revoke the certificate and publish the updated revocation list

appliesWhen: a key that is lost or compromised is still treated as valid
explanation: A lost or compromised key keeps working until it is revoked. Revoking it and updating the certificate revocation list stops any further use.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: the web server's private key file sits in a shared network folder
any staff member can open the folder
a copy of the site appeared on a fake server using the real certificate
the key file has no password

answer.cause: the private key is stored without protection where many people can read it
answer.action: Move the keys into a hardware security module or a secure key vault

appliesWhen: keys sit in a place that unauthorized people can read or copy
explanation: A private key that anyone can copy lets an attacker pose as the server. Keys belong in a hardware security module, key vault, or other protected store.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: an old server was sold to a recycler last month
files encrypted with the company's backup key have now been opened by an outsider
the backup key was retired when the server was replaced
the server's drive was only formatted before the sale

answer.cause: the retired key was never securely destroyed and was recovered from the old server
answer.action: Destroy retired keys securely and wipe drives before disposal

appliesWhen: a key that is no longer needed was left where it can be recovered
explanation: A key that is no longer used must be destroyed so it cannot be recovered. A quick format leaves data that can be read back, so the key and the drive must be wiped.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: a user plugged a small desk switch into the wall jack to add a printer
both the PC and the printer lost the network at once
the switch port shows err-disabled
the switch sent an SNMP trap about a new hardware address

answer.cause: a port security violation shut down the switch port
answer.action: Remove the extra device, then clear the violation and re-enable the port

firstStep: Check the switch port's status and its security log
appliesWhen: the switch saw more hardware addresses on a port than it allows
explanation: Port security limits how many hardware addresses a port accepts, and a second device on the port caused a violation. The switch then shut the port down.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: a new tablet sees the store's wireless network but cannot join it
the passphrase was typed correctly
the three older tablets connect with no problem
the access point only lets listed adapters connect

answer.cause: the new tablet's MAC address is not on the access point's allow list
answer.action: Add the new tablet's MAC address to the allow list

firstStep: Compare the tablet's hardware address with the access point's filter list
appliesWhen: a device's hardware address has not been added to the access point's filter
explanation: With MAC filtering, the access point accepts only adapters on its allow list, so a new device is rejected even with the right passphrase. Adding its hardware address lets it join.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: a laptop back from a long trip connects but can only reach the update server
other laptops on the same switch get full access
the laptop's antivirus definitions are four months old
the network places failing devices in a separate VLAN

answer.cause: the laptop failed the NAC posture assessment and was quarantined
answer.action: Update the antivirus definitions and patches, then reconnect

firstStep: Check the NAC server's report for the laptop
appliesWhen: a device was quarantined because its security state failed the check
explanation: NAC checks a device's security state when it connects and sends a device that fails to a quarantine network. Bringing the definitions and patches up to date lets it pass.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: one laptop is refused at every wired and wireless port
the RADIUS log shows the laptop's certificate has expired
other laptops sign in with EAP-TLS with no problem
the problem started on the first of the month

answer.cause: the laptop's client certificate has expired, so 802.1X authentication fails

firstStep: Read the RADIUS log entry for the laptop
appliesWhen: the device's certificate for EAP-TLS is no longer valid
explanation: With 802.1X using EAP-TLS, the authentication server checks the device's certificate, and an expired one is refused at every port. A new certificate lets the device authenticate again.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: a permit rule for the new web server was added yesterday
outside users still cannot reach the server
a rule that blocks the whole server subnet sits above the new rule
the firewall reads its rules from the top down

answer.cause: an explicit deny rule above the permit rule matches the traffic first
answer.action: Move the permit rule above the deny rule

firstStep: Read the firewall rules in order to see which one matches first
appliesWhen: an earlier deny entry in the list matches the traffic before the permit entry
explanation: Rules are read in order, and an explicit deny takes precedence, so the earlier block wins. Placing the narrower permit rule above it lets the traffic through.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: staff cannot open a supplier's ordering website
the browser shows a block page from the web proxy
the page says the site is in the gambling category
other websites open normally

answer.cause: the web filter has placed the supplier's site in a blocked category
answer.action: Add the supplier's site to the web filter's allow list

firstStep: Check the web filter's log for the supplier's site
appliesWhen: the web filter puts a legitimate site in a category that is blocked
explanation: URL filtering blocks sites by category, and a site placed in the wrong category is blocked with the rest. An allow entry for that one site fixes it without changing the category rule.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security

clues: a new reporting application uses TCP port 8443
clients time out when they connect to it through the firewall
the firewall log shows the traffic dropped by the last rule
no rule mentions port 8443

answer.cause: no permit rule exists for the new application's port, so the implicit deny drops it
answer.action: Add a permit rule for the application's port to the right server

firstStep: Check the firewall log for the dropped connections
appliesWhen: traffic is dropped because no rule allows it
explanation: Anything that no rule permits is caught by the implicit deny at the end of the rule set. A permit rule for that port and server lets the traffic pass.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 9: Network Security
